name: copy
summary: Out = In (ND contiguous, flattened numel). Variants: f32 and f16. Uses a simple 1D kernel with blocks capped at 4096.
contract: - X and Y same rank and same shape
- elementwise copy on flattened numel() (ND supported)
notes: numel_anyrank(): returns 0 if rank<=0 or any dim<=0; otherwise product(shape).
Launch config: threads=256, blocks=ceil(n/256), blocks clamped to [1,4096].
Contiguity is enforced via TensorDesc.contiguous (no stride-based contig inference).

variants.name: copy_f32
supported: X,Y same rank and same shape
notes: If n==0 => return Ok without launching.

variants.name: copy_f16
supported: X,Y same rank and same shape
notes: If n==0 => return Ok without launching.

suites.name: basic_nd_shapes
suites.desc: Common ND shapes for copy; verify dtype gating and correctness. Copy is memory-bound; measure latency/GB/s.

suites.name: edge_cases
suites.desc: Corner cases: n=0 and rank<=0 behavior as implemented by numel_anyrank().

cases.label: Any dim==0 -> numel==0 -> Ok without launch
rank<=0 -> numel_anyrank returns 0 (implementation-defined); should not launch

suites.name: supported_gating
suites.desc: Verify supported() rejects mismatch dtype/shape or non-contiguous.

experiments.title: Vectorized copy (ld/st v4)
experiments.change: Add a fastpath variant using vectorized loads/stores (e.g., int4/float4/half2/half4) when pointers are suitably aligned and numel divisible.
experiments.why: Plain scalar copy may underutilize memory transaction width; vectorization can improve effective bandwidth.
experiments.hypothesis: For large n, vectorized path increases GB/s and lowers latency vs scalar path.
experiments.proof: ncu: compare global load/store efficiency, memory throughput; verify correctness.
experiments.next: Add alignment gating: 16B for int4; consider cp.async for smem staging only if needed (usually not).

experiments.title: Use cudaMemcpyAsync for pure contiguous copy
experiments.change: Replace kernel launch with cudaMemcpyAsync for same-device contiguous copies when safe.
experiments.why: Kernel launch overhead dominates for small tensors; memcpy path may be faster and simpler.
experiments.hypothesis: Small/medium tensors see lower latency; large tensors similar bandwidth.
experiments.proof: Benchmark latency across sizes; ensure stream semantics match; validate behavior under graph capture if applicable.
experiments.next: Keep kernel fallback for special cases (non-standard alignment, future mixed dtype support, etc.).

measurements.notes: Copy is memory-bound; report latency and effective GB/s (bytes=2*n read + 2*n write).
